source.title: ISRU Pilot Excavator: Bucket drum scaling experimental results

conversion: Figure 13 mN/mm equals N/m exactly; width multiplier is one whole drum axial width in metres.

extraction.method: Least-squares line through colored dotted-trend pixels away from end-point data markers; evaluate at 10 and 30 mm/s.
extraction.resolution_note: Approximate pixel-coordinate resolution, not a statistical force uncertainty or instrument accuracy.

source_envelope.tip_ratio_tolerance_note: 1% bookkeeping allowance for published rounding; not a measured validity range.

limitations: Eight curve readings, not eight raw experimental trials. No individual run/size identities or measurement uncertainties are available from this plot.

Figure 13 labels depths 10, 12.7, 16, 25 mm. Table 2 says 10 mm and 40% scoop height; combined with Table 1 the latter would be 10.56, 13.8, 19.12 mm. This inconsistency is unresolved; the surface uses Figure 13 labels.

Depth, drum size and scoop geometry are confounded in the source design; the width-normalized plot is pooled across sizes. Rectangular parameter bounds do not establish support at every interior combination.
Speed and RPM were linked through tip/feed ratio 8.5. The data do not identify an independent RPM response.
Width scaling assumes source-like staggered scoop geometry. Our baseline width/diameter ratio differs from the source drums.
Published trend curves already fit their underlying measurements. Curve approximation or held-out-depth validation does not establish independent hardware validation.
Earth-gravity horizontal force only. No vertical load, tangential force, shaft torque, mean-to-peak conversion, counteracting-drum cancellation or material recirculation law is identified.

validation.strategy: Leave one complete depth series (both speeds) out of the fitting inputs for each of four folds. Also report in-sample curve approximation residuals.
